items.claim: The span 2:17-2:19 is one narrative movement and its onset at 2:16/2:17 is sound, but its close at 2:19/2:20 is argued from the onset side only. The last clause of 2:19 states that Daniel blessed the God of heaven, and the praise of 2:20-2:23 is that blessing spoken; the device inventory holds the blessing word on both sides of the seam (2:19 and 2:20), and the opening of 2:20 is the answered-and-said connective, which the book's rules treat as too weak to open a unit alone. The row grades itself medium while the row across the same seam is medium_low.
items.both_sides: Onset seam 2:16/2:17: before it, Daniel's request to the king ends and a PE follows 2:16 (single witness, WLC); after it, 2:17 opens with the then connective and a change of place to Daniel's house. Both sides agree. Close seam 2:19/2:20: before it, 2:19 ends on the narrator's statement that Daniel blessed God, which looks forward to the words of the blessing rather than closing the scene; after it, 2:20 has a speaker formula and a self-contained hymn in a different form. The form change supports the seam; the forward-looking close and the weak connective do not. No mark follows 2:19.

suggested_fix.fact: The close seam is weighed from both sides: the blessing announced in the last clause of 2:19 is delivered in 2:20-2:23, the blessing word stands on each side of the seam, and the speaker formula of 2:20 is a weak connective; the seam rests on the change of form alone, and the grade follows that.

items.claim: 2:36-2:45 is one interpretation and should stay one row, but the ground the row gives for rejecting a cut at 2:43/2:44 is not the ground that holds. The rule it cites concerns where a report parts from its interpretation (2:35/2:36); it says nothing about a cut inside the interpretation. What holds is in the text: 2:44 opens with a time phrase that depends on the kings of 2:37-2:43, and 2:45 returns to the stone of 2:34 and ends on the certainty formula, so 2:44-2:45 cannot stand apart. The row also exceeds nine verses and says it is a single speech act, but it does not say that no internal signal divides it, which is the condition for the exception; and its speech-act claim is loose, since Daniel's speech runs from 2:27 and is already divided at 2:30/2:31 and 2:35/2:36.
items.both_sides: Onset seam 2:35/2:36: before it the report ends; after it 2:36 names the dream and announces the interpretation. Close seam 2:45/2:46: before it, the certainty formula ends Daniel's speech and a PE follows 2:45 (single witness); after it, 2:46 opens with the then connective, a new actor and a reaction. Both sides agree at each edge. Rival 2:43/2:44: before it, 2:43 ends the reading of the iron and clay; after it, 2:44 depends on the kings just named and 2:45 completes the reading of the stone. The after side does not open a unit.

suggested_fix.fact: A cut at 2:43/2:44 is declined on the text: the time phrase that opens 2:44 refers to the kings of the verses before it, and 2:45 reads the stone of the report and closes on the certainty of dream and interpretation. The row states that no internal signal of a new unit stands inside 2:36-2:45, the time phrase at 2:44 being a link back.

items.claim: 2:46-2:49 is a sound closing narrative: the king's prostration, his confession, Daniel's promotion and the appointment of the three at Daniel's request, ending with Daniel at the king's gate. Keeping 2:49 inside the row is right, because 2:49 depends on the promotion of 2:48 and has no reach beyond the scene. The defect is in the wording of the ground: boundary_rationale says the chapter ends at 2:49. A chapter line may neither drive nor corroborate a seam, and the row has the text's own grounds to hand: the appointment notice of 2:49 and the subject-first royal clause of 3:1.
items.both_sides: Onset seam 2:45/2:46: before it, Daniel's speech ends on the certainty formula and a PE follows 2:45; after it, the then connective with the king as new actor. Close seam 2:49/3:1: before it, the appointment notice ends with Daniel's station and a PE follows 2:49 (single witness); after it, 3:1 opens with the king as subject making an image, a new action and object with no connective. Both sides agree at each edge.

suggested_fix.fact: The unit closes on the appointment of the three and Daniel's station at the king's gate at 2:49, and the next verse opens with a subject-first royal clause and a new action; the close is stated without reference to the chapter.

triage_answers.decision: Every tier word in the six rows was tested against the layer it names. No tier word names a layer that fails to hold a stated witness fact, with three low exceptions. (1) Language: each device_notes says MEASURED of the language; verse_language is A for all 33 verses of 2:17-2:49, so the language claim is true, but no script is named with MEASURED and, in five of the six rows (all but W1-012), the word sits beside a genre word the layer does not hold. (2) W1-010 boundary_rationale tiers 'stops the executions' as EXTRACTED from WEB; WEB 2:24 holds the request, and the stopping is a reading. (3) W1-012 boundary_rationale tiers 'the PE after 2:45 closes it' as EXTRACTED; the mark is extracted, the closing is a reading. Every EXTRACTED mark and ketiv/qere claim holds in both directions; W1-012's MEASURED ketiv/qere list is complete and exact; every INFERRED word sits on a reading; W1-009's REPORTED word on the two rival edges is true of the strategy's text.

triage_answers.decision: Note (e): yes, the genre word needs its own tier or the phrase needs recasting. In W1-008 (narrative), W1-009 (hymn), W1-010 (dialogue), W1-011 (report) and W1-013 (narrative close) the MEASURED word follows a phrase that joins language and genre, and a reader takes it to cover both; the layer holds the language only, and the genre is the row's reading. W1-012 already predicates the language alone and needs nothing. The fact to install in the five rows: the language of the span is measured from the language layer; the form is the row's reading. Note (f): W1-012's ketiv/qere list was tested against the mark layer and is complete and exact (2:38 to 2:43, six verses, no others in 2:36-2:45); W1-006 is outside this cluster. Note (d), second half: W1-010's last sentence of the rejected alternative carries INFERRED, and that is true of a weighing. Notes (a), (b), (c) and (d, first half) concern rows outside this cluster.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether a row's grade follows its weaker edge. W1-008 has a well-supported onset and a close argued from one side; I read the grading rule as letting the weaker edge govern.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If the grade is meant to describe the row's unit rather than its edges, W1-008's medium may stand and only the both-sides weighing is owed.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether row prose may cite the strategy's rulings, guards and regions by letter. Five of the six rows do (all but W1-008, whose rejected alternative still cites one ruling label); the suite raised no flag on this part.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If labels are not allowed in rows, the same low finding applies across the cluster and is a part-wide rewording, not six separate ones.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether OSHB editorial notes and paseq owe disclosure in every row whose span holds one. The mark layer's own note says the editorial notes are to be disclosed; the paseq layer is count-only. I raised the editorial notes at 2:29 and 2:31 and only mentioned the paseq at 2:23, 2:24 and 2:35.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It decides whether W1-010 and W1-011 carry a defect or a courtesy gap, and whether three more rows owe a paseq mention.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the time phrase at 2:44 counts as an internal signal for the over-nine-verse exception. I read it as a link back to the kings of 2:37-2:43, not an onset.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If it counts, W1-012 does not meet the exception as stated and a cut at 2:43/2:44 would have to be weighed in earnest.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: MEASURED without a named script in the language and ketiv/qere annotations. I confirmed the facts by my own scans; I did not see the writers' scripts.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The facts are true, but the tier form the strategy asks for (a script with MEASURED) is not met, and I cannot say whether the fix-up's fixed grammar allowed one.
